_comment: A `tbzl.buildconfig/v1` document for tbzl-boston, the bare-metal plane.
⚠ SCRUBBED AND NON-EXECUTABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: this contains no secret and cannot.
The protocol carries a token URL, a scope and an issuer — the coordinates for MINTING
a credential — and never a credential. A served profile is cached, logged by
--announce_rc and attached to build records, so anything secret here would be secret
⛔ The exec-property container-image is an opaque ROUTING TOKEN the scheduler
string-compares and NEVER fetches. It is 394050190195 here and 042825952740 on the AWS
plane, and that difference is REAL: it changed with this cutover, unlike the previous
one. Pointing at the wrong account names a platform NO WORKER SERVES, and the scheduler
rejects with 'No workers exist for instance name prefix' — which reads as a dead plane.

recommendations.basis: observational/2026-08-19.1 — NOT a tuning study, and deliberately not copied from the AWS profile. jobs=64 is the value savvifi/aion already used for the first green build on this plane (31443 processes, 14474 remote, 0 local, 946s wall, critical path 464s); it is carried forward because it is known to work here, not because it was shown to be optimal. ⚠ The AWS profile recommends 200 from a measured study on a fleet that autoscaled to 150 workers; this box is ONE node with worker concurrency 32, so that number does not transfer and copying it would oversubscribe a fixed pool. ⏰ Raise this only from a measurement on this plane — concurrency sitting at exactly 64 while the worker has free slots is the signal that --jobs is binding.
